responsibility: This is the main implementation file for the GCC eBPF target backend. It defines target attributes such as kernel_helper and preserve_access_index, registers and resolves BPF-specific builtins including non-generic packet loads and CO-RE builtins, performs option override and per-function machine-state setup, implements core target hooks used by code generation (calls, prologue/epilogue, operand printing, branch expansion, target macros, frame handling), and contains the BPF-specific RTL pass that scans preserve_access_index accesses and emits CO-RE relocation requests for later .BTF.ext output.
same_name_distinction: Unlike the other same-stem BPF files, this is the executable C++ backend implementation: it wires the target hooks declared/configured by the port, handles BPF-specific attributes and builtins, and runs the CO-RE relocation discovery pass. The sibling files instead provide static target macros (bpf.h), RTL instruction patterns (bpf.md), or option definitions for generated flag handling (bpf.opt).
